tier_reason: Raised D to B. Enricher e127 (2026-10-05) read the camera-ready LaTeX of the peer-reviewed paper (PACMPL vol. 10, OOPSLA2, October 2026, article 339) in the first author's public repo github.com/bhargavkulk/skia-paper (evaluation.tex, macros.tex via raw.githubusercontent.com). The catalogued 18.7% / 99 programs / 32 us figures were the arXiv v1 abstract; the final evaluation reports a 1.12x geomean on 139 SaveLayer-bearing Skia pictures with stated hardware, compiler, flags, Skia commit and methodology. Not A: the optimizer code and Skia fork are only on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.21386615, blocked here) and not upstreamed, so the benchmark is not reproducible from public GitHub sources.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Peer-reviewed (OOPSLA2 2026, final evaluation): 1.12x geomean (max 3.04x) on 139 SaveLayer-bearing Skia pictures captured from Chrome on the top 100 sites, Graphite/Metal backend on an Apple M2, nanobench median of 25 runs with bootstrap 95% CI; Ganesh on the M2 1.08x; Intel i7-8700K with CoffeeLake-S GT2 1.14x (Graphite) and 1.07x (Ganesh) on 143 recaptured pictures; the next 100 sites 1.18x on 144 pictures with the passes frozen; optimisation time at most 0.03 ms per picture. The arXiv v1 abstract's 18.7% over 99 programs and 32 us optimisation time are superseded.
corrections.hardware: 8-core Apple M2 (16 GB), Graphite/Metal and Ganesh backends; Intel i7-8700K with CoffeeLake-S GT2 integrated GPU.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Skia f931a2e built with Clang 17.0.0 -O3 -flto=thin (M2); Clang 18.1.3 on the Intel machine; nanobench, median of 25 runs with bootstrap confidence intervals.
corrections.caveats: Final paper read from the camera-ready LaTeX (bhargavkulk/skia-paper); the ACM DOI 10.1145/3839471, arXiv 2603.23696 and Zenodo are egress-blocked here. Only 51 of the 139 pictures are rewritten at all (38 with a confidence interval above 1x), so the 1.12x geomean includes unrewritten noise; the benchmark is per-layer skp playback in nanobench, not page frame time; 25 of 139 outputs differ from Skia by more than 1% of pixels; four significant slowdowns on the Intel machine. The optimizer is a rewrite pass in front of Skia (removing redundant layers and state changes in Chrome's command streams), not a rasterizer; the formal semantics is in Lean. Code and the Skia fork are only in the Zenodo artifact 10.5281/zenodo.21386615 (not on GitHub, not upstreamed), so has_code stays false.
